description: The bar chart illustrates the average change in the INC score from the combined layer to the base layer, with negative values indicating that the base layer outperformed the combined layer and positive values indicating the opposite. The horizontal axis represents the observation probability, ranging from 0.2 to 0.9, while the vertical axis shows the average change in the INC score, scaled from -3 to 2. Two types of inputs are compared: inferred frames, represented by gray bars, and lexical signals, represented by orange bars. At each observation probability level, the gray bars are consistently negative, indicating that the base layer performs better when using inferred frames. In contrast, the orange bars are positive across all levels, indicating that the combined layer performs better when using lexical signals. The height of the bars varies, with the most negative change (strongest base layer performance) occurring at an observation probability of 0.2 for inferred frames, and the most positive change (strongest combined layer performance) occurring at 0.5 for lexical signals. The chart visually supports the caption’s claim that inferred frames favor the base layer, while lexical signals enhance the combined layer’s performance.
